parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.stem: Magnesium nitrate, $\text{Mg(NO}_3)_2$, is very soluble in water. When a hot saturated solution of magnesium nitrate is cooled, crystals of the hydrate, $\text{Mg(NO}_3)_2\cdot 6\text{H}_2\text{O}$, are formed. In the crystals, six water molecules bond to each $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ ion, and some of these water molecules are **also** bonded to the nitrate ions.
parts.text: Suggest the type of bonding that occurs between $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ and $\text{NO}_3^-$.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Describe the arrangement of the water molecules around the $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ ion.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text: Describe in detail what you would observe when crystals of $\text{Mg(NO}_3)_2\cdot 6\text{H}_2\text{O}$ are heated in a boiling tube, gently at first and then more strongly. Write equations for any reactions that occur.

parts.label: (a)(iv)
parts.text: Calculate the percentage **loss** in mass when $\text{Mg(NO}_3)_2\cdot 6\text{H}_2\text{O}$ is heated strongly to constant mass.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain why the Group 2 nitrates become more stable to heat down the group.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Magnesium nitrate and silver nitrate, $\text{AgNO}_3$, decompose on heating to produce the same gases. Silver nitrate also produces silver metal during decomposition.
parts.text: Write an equation for the decomposition of $\text{AgNO}_3$.
